findings.evidenceType: manual source-pixel visual plus sampled browser
findings.finding: Enlarged awake crop has a round black eye aperture, rim and distinct bright catchlight. Closed crop has a horizontal narrow lid and lacks the open aperture. At about52worldpx bird width, eye detail is necessarily tiny but the brief state change is readable in the sampled output. This is an actual new eye drawing, not inferred from prompt or source hash.

Dark hood, warm brown back, buff flanks, pale belly, pink conical bill, pink feet and narrow white tail-edge accents support the intended Oregon-type Junco reading. New pair remains visually compatible with the earlier generated rest reference; exact anatomical/sex/subspecies fidelity is not expert-certified. Reference whole-canvas thumbnail is differently registered/scaled, so it was not used as a numerical size-matching test.

findings.evidenceType: manual actual-size source and browser raster inspection
findings.finding: Dark head remains legible against the pale preview background, with compact brown wing and pale belly regions. Fine feather texture is present on enlargement; no conspicuous random pale interior sparkle or large brightness flash was apparent between the two sampled actual-size states. This does not diagnose the unseen Mac screenshot or guarantee appearance against every yard background.

findings.evidenceType: manual enlarged contact inspection plus independent fixed-ROI heuristic
findings.finding: Both drawings have plausible short legs and spread clawed toes. Small claw tips and nearby feather edges redraw. No gross dislocated foot, extra major limb or whole-body jump was apparent in the reviewed states. This is not tracked anatomical toe locking.

findings.evidenceType: decoded APNG durations and timestamped browser samples
findings.finding: APNG durations are2000/100/900ms, matching60/3/27 ticks at30Hz. Samples include open, closed, open and a later open state after the3s boundary. First and last use the same awake source; body-pixel equality between natural drawings is not a quality gate. A two-drawing100ms blink is brief and useful; no half-lid drawing or broader action is claimed.
